name: Facial thread lift (cheek lifting)

lead: A thread lift uses threads inserted under the skin to lift the cheeks and midface without cutting away skin.
Trials are registered, but published outcome data were not available in the sources reviewed.

paras: Threads, some barbed or coated, anchor and elevate tissue, and are placed through small entry points.
Physician and media reports describe infection, vessel puncture and pain, and some threads cannot easily be removed. Practitioner qualifications vary by country.

lead: A thread lift is a non-surgical or minimally invasive procedure in which threads, some with barbs or cones, are placed under the skin to lift facial tissue without removing skin.[1] Applied to the cheeks, it is used to raise the midface and soften the nasolabial fold.[2]

Wikipedia describes it as a simplified alternative to a facelift and reports physician and media concerns about complications and about training standards.[1] Two registered trials exist, one comparing hyaluronic acid-coated and non-coated threads for the midface and one combining threads with microfocused ultrasound.[2][3] Results were not available in the sources reviewed.

paras: Wikipedia reports that one physician has called it among the riskiest procedures an aesthetic practitioner can perform, noting that some threads stay in the tissue and cannot be pulled out, and that a 2021 BBC investigation of training courses recorded poor infection control and severe patient pain.[1] The article also notes UK aesthetic practitioners needed no mandatory qualifications.[1]

A completed 144-participant registered study (NCT07916103, started 2024) compared HA-coated and non-HA threads for midface lifting and nasolabial fold correction.[2] A 45-participant registration (NCT04157218, started 2019, status unknown) examined thread lifting with microfocused ultrasound.[3] No published results were in the sources reviewed.
